title: Speech capabilities and user benefits · Level 2
slo: Explain what speech recognition and speech synthesis do and how they support users.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe speech synthesis? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Text-to-speech is a name for synthesis. It describes text becoming audio.
TTS abbreviates text-to-speech. It refers to speech synthesis.
Synthesis produces spoken audio for a listener. It can communicate written information aloud.
Transcription creates written text from spoken words. That is recognition's role.
options.better_fit: It fits meeting-note or call-transcription systems.

feedback.intrinsic: A listener would not receive spoken information.
feedback.instructional: Synthesis speaks text; recognition transcribes speech.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Synthesis is TTS and provides spoken output.

exercises.question_text: Which are speech capabilities? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Speech recognition is a speech capability. It converts spoken words to text.
Speech synthesis is a speech capability. It converts text to spoken audio.
Text-to-speech is another name for synthesis. It speaks written information.
Audio capture supplies a digital audio signal. It does not itself convert between speech and text.
options.better_fit: It is an early step before recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: Captured audio alone produces neither transcript nor response.
feedback.instructional: Recognition and synthesis are the conversion capabilities.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition and synthesis are speech capabilities.

exercises.question_text: The capability that turns written text into natural-sounding spoken audio is ___.

parts.text: The capability that turns written text into natural-sounding spoken audio is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The application would not provide the needed spoken message.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Recognition creates text from speech; synthesis creates audio from text.

exercises.explanation: Speech synthesis, also called TTS, converts written text into natural-sounding spoken audio.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the two capabilities becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the shared relationship, then identify each capability's role.

exercises.correct_answer: Two capabilities work in opposite directions Recognition receives speech synthesis produces audio
exercises.explanation: Recognition handles spoken input, while synthesis creates spoken output; their directions are opposite.

exercises.question_text: A navigation app must announce directions while drivers keep their eyes on the road. Which capability should its developer choose?

options.rationale: Directions are written information that must be announced aloud. Synthesis converts that text into audio.
Recognition can understand a driver's command. It does not speak directions aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: Drivers would not hear the next turn.

options.rationale: Capture receives sound from a microphone. It cannot generate a spoken direction.

feedback.intrinsic: The app could listen but not announce.

options.rationale: Language modeling helps choose likely word sequences. It does not create an audio waveform.

feedback.instructional: Use speech synthesis for spoken navigation.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Synthesis turns direction text into spoken guidance.

exercises.question_text: A voice-service team needs callers to speak questions and hear spoken answers. Which plan should the designer choose?

options.rationale: Recognition converts callers' speech into text. Synthesis speaks the response text aloud.
Recognition understands the caller's spoken question. It cannot produce a spoken reply.
options.better_fit: It fits a service that only needs written call records.

feedback.intrinsic: The caller would not hear an answer.
feedback.instructional: Two-way voice interaction needs recognition for input and synthesis for output.

options.rationale: Synthesis can speak a prepared response. It cannot understand the caller's question.
options.better_fit: It fits an app that only announces information.

feedback.intrinsic: The service would not know what the caller asked.
feedback.instructional: Recognition is needed to process spoken requests.

options.rationale: Capture records sound as data. It neither transcribes questions nor speaks answers.
options.better_fit: It fits the input stage before recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: The call could be recorded without becoming a voice conversation.
feedback.instructional: Capture is not a replacement for recognition and synthesis.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The service needs both speech directions.

exercises.question_text: An app uses ___ when it turns spoken words into written text.

parts.text: when it turns spoken words into written text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The app would not create the required transcript.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Synthesis speaks text; recognition transcribes speech.

exercises.explanation: Speech recognition, or speech-to-text, converts spoken words into written text.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the action, then name the input and output alternatives.

exercises.correct_answer: Always provide text-based input and output alternatives
exercises.explanation: Accessible speech applications provide both text-based input and output alternatives.

exercises.question_text: A supervisor needs real-time written call records for quality review. Which components should the team use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The call audio must first enter the system. Capture provides the signal recognition analyzes.
Recognition converts the captured call into text. That text forms the written record.
Speech-to-text is another name for recognition. It directly supports real-time transcription.
Synthesis creates spoken audio from text. It does not create the written records requested.
options.better_fit: It fits a phone service that speaks answers.

feedback.intrinsic: The supervisor would still lack a transcript.
feedback.instructional: For written call records, capture speech and use recognition.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Capture supplies audio and recognition produces text.

exercises.question_text: Supporting multiple languages and regional dialects can improve an application's ___.

parts.text: Supporting multiple languages and regional dialects can improve an application's

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Users in additional regions could remain unsupported.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Language and dialect support specifically expands global reach.

exercises.explanation: Language and dialect support helps an application serve audiences in more places, improving global reach.

exercises.question_text: A language-learning app lets students speak phrases and hear corrections, but some learners need non-speech access. What should the designer also provide?

options.rationale: Some learners prefer or require non-speech interaction. Text alternatives keep both practice and feedback accessible.
Voice-only controls create barriers for learners who cannot use speech. They do not provide a non-speech route.
options.better_fit: They fit students who choose to practice by speaking.

feedback.intrinsic: Some learners could not complete the activity.
feedback.instructional: Keep a text-based way to participate.

options.rationale: Natural voices improve spoken output quality. They do not provide text access for non-speech users.

feedback.intrinsic: A learner needing text would still lack access.
feedback.instructional: Voice quality matters, but text output is the required alternative.

options.rationale: Dialect support helps serve language varieties. It does not replace alternative input and output methods.
options.better_fit: It fits a goal of broader language coverage.

feedback.intrinsic: Non-speech learners could still face barriers.
feedback.instructional: Support dialects when needed and also provide text alternatives.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Text alternatives make the experience usable without speech.

exercises.question_text: A clinical professional must update notes while continuing patient care. Which speech benefits matter most? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Speaking can reduce keyboard use during care. This supports hands-free operation.
The professional can document while care continues. That is multitasking.
Speaking notes can reduce interruptions to care. It can feel more natural than stopping to type.
Text input should remain available as an alternative. It does not provide the main speech benefit in this situation.
options.better_fit: It fits a non-speech access method.

feedback.intrinsic: The professional would need to stop and type.
feedback.instructional: Keep text alternatives, but speech supports hands-free documentation here.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech can support hands-free work and multitasking.
